newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen Dev Bank plans rights offer.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen Dev Bank plans rights offer.

text.p: Blue-chip issue Shenzhen Development Bank Ltd said on Thursday that it plans to make a 1.5-for-10 rights offer, and the proposal would be approved by shareholders at an upcoming meeting.
The offer would be priced at 8.00 yuan per rights share and launched by April of 1997, the firm said in a notice published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
On Thursday, the bank's class A shares closed at 14.99 yuan per share.
Shareholders are slated to vote on the plan at a meeting scheduled for October 15, the Shenzhen-listed bank said.
The rights offer also requires the final approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
Development Bank said it aims to use proceeds from the rights issue to expand its banking network in China and to renovate banking facilities.
The bank said recently in its interim report that a sharp surge in first-half net profits for 1996 was based on its success in expanding its operations.

In a report published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times, the bank said that under Chinese accounting standards, it chalked up audited net earnings of 364.23 million yuan in the first half of 1996, compared with 216.50 million yuan in the year-ago period.
The company, the sole bank listed in China, said the steep rise in its first-half profits was fueled in part by a 61.53 percent surge in earnings derived from its foreign exchange business.
The sector generated net profits of US$24.10 million, equivalent to 200.52 million yuan, in the first half, accounting for 46.92 percent of the bank's 1996 interim net.
Shenzhen Development Bank said in its annual report for 1995 that it had after-tax profits of 435.13 million yuan last year, compared with 356.33 million yuan in the previous year.
